title: Kapoor Singh Governs Through Collective Discipline

blocks.text: Life at Akal Takht continues under Kapoor Singh with an emphasis on humility and shared deliberation. He does not behave like an isolated courtly ruler, but keeps authority tied to the congregation and to Panthic consultation.

Administrative order now becomes visible in practical terms. Whatever money entered the Sikh coffers was treated as common wealth, gathered into approved channels, and entrusted to named servants responsible for stores, kitchens, weapons, and other necessities of the community.

The page closes by linking institution to discipline. Service roles are honored, supplies are regulated, and Singhs who leave without permission cannot casually return; they must first undergo the punishment that restores accountability within the Panth.
